sections.title: The Body and the Doctor
sections.content: A check-up needs the parts being checked and the people doing the checking. Note that Spanish uses the definite article with body parts where English uses a possessive: the doctor listens to 'el corazón', looks at 'los ojos' — not 'his heart', 'his eyes'. Whose they are is obvious, so Spanish does not say it.

sections.title: The body, and what people do

items.spanish: El médico examina al bebé y escucha su corazón.
items.english: The doctor examines the baby and listens to his heart.

items.spanish: En la sala de espera hay muchas familias con niños pequeños.
items.english: In the waiting room there are lots of families with small children.

items.spanish: Todo está muy bien. El bebé está sano.
items.english: Everything's fine. The baby is healthy.

items.spanish: Hablamos sobre la importancia de cuidar la salud.
items.english: We talk about how important it is to look after your health.

sections.content: 'El oído' is the ear you hear with, on the inside; the ear you can see is 'la oreja'. A doctor checks 'los oídos'.
